rationale: exptree is a tiny (14 functions, ~2.6 KB text) but recursion- and search-heavy benchmark (recSearch, doSearch, queens-style backtracking), so the weight table favors low-cost, correctness-safe passes that apply broadly while penalizing expensive transforms on hot recursive paths. SUB and SPLIT get high weights with the highest CorrectnessRisk sensitivity because they are cheap, semantics-preserving workhorses suited to many small functions; FLA is weighted highest for SecurityGain since the two largest functions (recSearch, getInput) have enough basic blocks for flattening to pay off, but a high RuntimeCost weight keeps it off tight recursive kernels. BCF carries the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights because bogus-control-flow bloat is most damaging in a program this small and hot; IBR and ICALL get strong SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights since indirect branch/call dispatch adds real static-analysis resistance at moderate cost, with CorrectnessRisk held high to restrict them to functions where indirecting is provably safe. IGV is omitted entirely: with only 14 functions forming a recursive, cross-file call graph, interprocedural virtualization risks correctness and code-size blowup for little marginal security over IBR+ICALL.
